source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which position relieves low back pain in a client with a herniated lumbar disk?
questions.rationale: Semi-Fowler's with the knees flexed (Williams position) relaxes the lower back muscles and relieves pressure on the spinal nerve root.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q7 (PDF p. 144)
questions.quote: This relaxes the muscles of the lower back and relieves pressure on the spinal nerve root.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Mario, 30, fractured his right ankle in a basketball game. A short leg plaster cast is applied in the emergency room.
questions.stem: Which home instruction BEST prevents complications?
options: Trim the rough edges when dry
Bear weight once it feels dry
Use a hanger to scratch inside
questions.rationale: Elevation increases venous return and reduces edema, which can cause compartment syndrome. Trimmed edges can fall into the cast, and scratching damages the skin.
explanations: Pieces can fall inside the cast.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q9 (PDF p. 147)
questions.quote: Leg elevation is important to increase venous return and decrease edema.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Mario, 30, fractured his right ankle in a basketball game. A short leg plaster cast is applied in the emergency room.
questions.stem: Which finding should make Mario seek medical attention right away?
options: A heavy, damp cast in the first day
questions.rationale: Numbness, tingling, and increased pain signal rising pressure from edema, which risks nerve damage. A cast takes up to 48 hours to dry and gives off heat while drying.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q702 (PDF p. 924)
questions.quote: Signs/symptoms of increased pressure from the cast include numbness, tingling, and increased pain.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Mario, 30, fractured his right ankle in a basketball game. A short leg plaster cast is applied in the emergency room.
questions.stem: Which statement shows Mario understands plaster cast care?
options: 'I'll cover it with a warm blanket.'
'I'll scratch under it with a ruler.'
questions.rationale: A plaster cast must stay dry to keep its strength. Air should circulate to help it dry, and it is handled with the palms.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1209 (PDF p. 1502)
questions.quote: A plaster cast must remain dry to keep its strength.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding suggests infection under a cast?
questions.rationale: Infection under a cast shows as a musty odor, purulent drainage, or warm areas on the cast. Edema, weak pulses, and cool pale skin signal impaired circulation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q46 (PDF p. 185)
questions.quote: Manifestations of infection under a casted area include a musty odor or purulent drainage from the cast or the presence of areas on the cast that are warmer than others.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which otoscopic finding does the nurse expect in mastoiditis?
questions.rationale: Mastoiditis shows a red, dull, thick, immobile tympanic membrane. The other findings are normal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q68 (PDF p. 213)
questions.quote: Otoscopic examination of a client with mastoiditis reveals a red, dull, thick, and immobile tympanic membrane

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which finding is MOST common in inner ear disorders?
questions.rationale: Tinnitus is the most common complaint in ear disorders, especially inner ear disorders. It ranges from mild ringing to a loud roaring.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q69 (PDF p. 214)
questions.quote: Tinnitus is the most common complaint of clients with ear disorders, especially disorders involving the inner ear.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Lola Iska, 78, is in Buck's extension traction after a hip fracture while awaiting surgery.
questions.stem: A complete neurovascular check of the affected leg includes:
questions.rationale: A neurovascular assessment covers color, sensation, movement, capillary refill, and pulses of the affected extremity.
explanations: Correct: the components of the check.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q122 (PDF p. 272)
questions.quote: A complete neurovascular assessment of an extremity includes color, sensation, movement, capillary refill, and pulse of the affected extremity.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Lola Iska, 78, is in Buck's extension traction after a hip fracture while awaiting surgery.
questions.stem: How does the nurse provide countertraction to reduce shear and friction?
options: Raise the foot of the bed slightly
Raise the head of the bed slightly
questions.rationale: The part of the bed under the traction is elevated. For leg traction, raising the foot of the bed opposes the traction force safely.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q151 (PDF p. 301)
questions.quote: For the client in skin traction (which is applied to a leg), the foot of the bed is elevated.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.situation: Lola Iska, 78, is in Buck's extension traction after a hip fracture while awaiting surgery.
questions.stem: Lola Iska becomes disoriented. What is the MOST appropriate action?
questions.rationale: Inactive older adults may become disoriented from lack of sensory stimulation. Frequent reorientation, with a clock and calendar in the room, helps. Restraints worsen disorientation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q882 (PDF p. 1122)
questions.quote: The appropriate nursing intervention would be to frequently reorient the client

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which pin-site finding is NORMAL in skeletal traction?
questions.rationale: A small amount of clear drainage ('weeping') can be expected. Loose pins, pus, redness, and swelling are reported.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q121 (PDF p. 271)
questions.quote: A small amount of clear drainage (“weeping”) may be expected after cleaning and removing crusting around the pin sites

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should the nurse handle a newly applied wet arm cast during transfer?
options: Put ice on top of it
questions.rationale: Palms or flat fingers prevent dents in a wet cast, and pillows support its curves so it does not crack or flatten.
explanations: Not on top of the cast.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q123 (PDF p. 273)
questions.quote: The palms or the flat surface of the extended fingers should be used when moving a wet cast to prevent indentations.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client asks why compartment syndrome developed after an arm fracture. What should the nurse explain?
options: A bone piece cut a nerve
questions.rationale: Bleeding and swelling inside a compartment lined by non-expanding fascia compress the nerves, muscles, and vessels within it.
explanations: Correct: pressure in a closed space.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q165 (PDF p. 317)
questions.quote: Compartment syndrome is caused by bleeding and swelling within a compartment, which is lined by fascia that does not expand.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which neurovascular finding with a new cast needs close follow-up?
questions.rationale: Normal capillary refill is under 3 seconds. Slow refill means poor circulation, and the toes or fingers will look pale or bluish.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q196 (PDF p. 350)
questions.quote: Optimally, the color will change from white to pink rapidly (less than 3 seconds).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which question helps assess for Ménière's disease?
options: 'Do you have ringing in your ears?'
questions.rationale: Ménière's disease involves excess endolymphatic fluid. It causes tinnitus, vertigo that can last for days, and one-sided sensorineural hearing loss.
explanations: Correct: tinnitus is a key sign.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q223 (PDF p. 378)
questions.quote: Manifestations include tinnitus, vertigo that can last for days, and one-sided sensorineural hearing loss.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet does the nurse expect to teach a client with Ménière's disease?
questions.rationale: Salt and fluid restrictions reduce the amount of endolymphatic fluid and are sometimes prescribed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1129 (PDF p. 1414)
questions.quote: Dietary changes such as salt and fluid restrictions that reduce the amount of endolymphatic fluid are sometimes prescribed

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which intervention helps a client with Ménière's syndrome control vertigo?
questions.rationale: Slow head movements prevent worsening vertigo. Clients are advised to stop smoking entirely because of its vasoconstrictive effects.
explanations: Smoking should stop, not be reduced.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1151 (PDF p. 1438)
questions.quote: The nurse instructs the client to make slow head movements to prevent worsening of the vertigo.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which instruction is MOST important for home safety in a client with chronic vertigo?
options: Turn only your head when spoken to
questions.rationale: Slipping and trying to regain balance can trigger vertigo, so clutter and throw rugs are removed. The client turns the whole body and changes position slowly.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q589 (PDF p. 797)
questions.quote: The client should maintain the home in a clutter-free state and have thrown rugs removed

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is an EARLY sign of rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.rationale: RA is a systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease. Early signs include fatigue, anorexia, weakness, low-grade fever, joint inflammation, and paresthesias. Deformities come later.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q349 (PDF p. 517)
questions.quote: Early manifestations include fatigue, anorexia, weakness, joint inflammation, low-grade fever

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which action ensures a client's traction is safe and effective?
options: Weights hanging free off the floor
questions.rationale: Weights must hang freely, with knots kept away from the pulleys. The head of the bed is usually kept low for countertraction.
explanations: Weights must not rest on anything.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q519 (PDF p. 714)
questions.quote: To achieve proper traction, weights need to be free-hanging, with knots kept away from the pulleys.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: On day 1 after total knee replacement, the client goes to a chair. How should the nurse protect the joint?
questions.rationale: A knee immobilizer stabilizes the joint, and the leg is elevated while sitting to minimize edema.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q574 (PDF p. 779)
questions.quote: the nurse assists the client to get out of bed on the first postoperative day after putting a knee immobilizer on the affected joint

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which surgeon's order needs clarification 2 hours after total knee surgery?
questions.rationale: Right after surgery the knee is kept in extension with a compression dressing. An order to keep it flexed needs clarification.
explanations: Correct answer: the knee is kept extended.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1382 (PDF p. 1685)
questions.quote: The knee is immobilized by a compression dressing to keep the knee in extension immediately after the operation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement after a total knee replacement shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'The knee's shape may change; that's normal.'
'I'll tell caregivers about my metal implant.'
questions.rationale: Any change in the knee's shape must be reported; it is not expected. The client informs caregivers of the implant, which requires antibiotic prophylaxis for invasive procedures.
explanations: Correct answer: shape changes must be reported.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1494 (PDF p. 1803)
questions.quote: After a total knee replacement, the client should be taught to report any changes in the shape of the knee.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement after total hip arthroplasty shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I won't twist my body when standing.'
'I can cross my legs when sitting.'
questions.rationale: Hip precautions include not crossing the legs past midline, avoiding bending past 90 degrees and twisting, and not sitting or standing for long periods.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q629 (PDF p. 846)
questions.quote: avoiding crossing the legs beyond the midline of the body

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client with a below-knee amputation understands residual limb care?
questions.rationale: The residual limb is inspected daily for irritation, blisters, and breakdown. A clean woolen sock is worn daily, and alcohol is avoided because it dries the skin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q603 (PDF p. 814)
questions.quote: The client should inspect all surfaces of the residual limb daily for irritation, blisters, and breakdown.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After LEFT eye cataract surgery, how should the client sleep?
options: On the right side or back
questions.rationale: The client sleeps on the nonoperative side or back to prevent edema. Bending below the waist or lowering the head raises intraocular pressure.
explanations: Correct: the nonoperative side or back.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q693 (PDF p. 914)
questions.quote: the client is informed to sleep on the nonoperative side or his or her back.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client asks what happens in polymyositis. The nurse explains that:
questions.rationale: Polymyositis is a diffuse inflammatory disorder of skeletal muscle causing symmetrical weakness and atrophy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q747 (PDF p. 975)
questions.quote: Polymyositis is a diffuse inflammatory disorder of skeletal (striated) muscle

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which behavior shows successful adaptation to presbycusis?
questions.rationale: Presbycusis is progressive age-related sensorineural hearing loss. Getting and regularly using a hearing aid shows good adaptation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q874 (PDF p. 1111)
questions.quote: Clients show adequate adaptation by obtaining and regularly using a hearing aid.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A day after hip implant surgery, a businessman is surrounded by work papers planning a meeting. What should guide the nurse's discussion?
options: Rest is essential for bone healing
Work keeps his mind off pain
He must stop all work now
questions.rationale: Rest is essential for bone healing, and stress should be minimized. Nurses encourage clients to balance work demands rather than demanding changes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q890 (PDF p. 1132)
questions.quote: Rest is an essential component of bone healing.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client in halo traction says, 'I can't see to the side and keep misjudging where things are.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
questions.rationale: Empathy and reflection, followed by a practical strategy, help the client adapt to limited peripheral vision.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q940 (PDF p. 1184)
questions.quote: In option 3, the nurse employs empathy and reflection. The nurse then offers a strategy for problem-solving

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After ventilation tubes are placed in the eardrum, which statement shows understanding?
questions.rationale: Water must be kept out of the ears. A shower cap or earplugs are used, and swimming and hair washing are avoided after surgery.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1069 (PDF p. 1351)
questions.quote: After the insertion of tubes into the tympanic membrane, it is important to avoid getting water in the ears.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An adult has a left earache, nausea, ear fullness, and fever. What should the nurse ask FIRST?
options: 'Do you clean your ears with cotton buds?'
questions.rationale: Adult otitis media is usually one-sided and acute, with earache, nausea, fever, and fullness. It often follows an upper respiratory infection, so the history is taken first.
explanations: Correct: URI often precedes otitis media.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1095 (PDF p. 1378)
questions.quote: Otitis media in the adult is typically one-sided and presents as an acute process with earache; nausea; and possible vomiting, fever, and fullness in the ear.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client is found on the floor after a fall, with a possible broken arm. What should the nurse do IMMEDIATELY?
questions.rationale: A suspected fracture must be splinted before the client is moved. Vital signs follow, and the provider is called.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1201 (PDF p. 1493)
questions.quote: When a fracture is suspected, it is imperative that the area be splinted before the client is moved.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which observation shows a successful outcome for a client in traction who is relearning self-care?
options: He does as much self-care as he can
He waits for staff to do it
questions.rationale: The goal is for the client to perform as much self-care as possible given the condition. The nurse promotes independence.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1243 (PDF p. 1536)
questions.quote: A successful outcome for reassuming self-care is for the client to do as much of the self-care as possible.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client's skin at the cast edge is pink and irritated. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Petaling the cast edges with tape minimizes skin irritation. Powder can clump and cause breakdown.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1433 (PDF p. 1742)
questions.quote: The nurse should petal the edges of the cast with tape to minimize skin irritation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is a comminuted fracture?
questions.rationale: A comminuted fracture is a complete break across the shaft with the bone splintered into fragments. A greenstick fracture is incomplete.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1533 (PDF p. 1844)
questions.quote: A comminuted fracture is a complete fracture across the shaft of a bone, with splintering of the bone into fragments.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which sign in a fractured arm indicates IMPAIRED VENOUS RETURN?
questions.rationale: Increasing edema marks impaired venous return and is prevented by elevation. Weak pulses and pallor suggest arterial damage.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1535 (PDF p. 1846)
questions.quote: Impaired venous return is characterized by increasing edema.
